methodology: Each record points to a public primary-source government record. Records are examples of denial, lapse, delay, extension, or approval-path friction; they are not statistical failure probabilities and do not imply that every referenced project ultimately failed.

records.agency: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
records.observed: The Board denied a variance application seeking to legalize an existing single-family residence that did not comply with front- and side-yard requirements. The decision discussed self-created hardship and builder error in declining relief.
records.lesson: Do not assume completed or hard-to-reverse work can later be regularized through discretionary relief. Verify the governing constraint before irreversible construction.

records.agency: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
records.observed: The time to complete construction under the variance expired. The applicant sought another extension and represented that pandemic effects and resulting financial issues delayed the project; the Board also asked for detail on permitting status and the construction timeline.
records.lesson: Entitlement clocks, permitting, financing, and construction sequencing interact. A project can retain conceptual feasibility while timing failure creates another approval dependency.

records.agency: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
records.status: Extension requested after construction deadline expired
records.observed: A 2026 public-hearing notice states that the applicant sought an extension of time to complete construction of a previously approved variance after the construction period expired on January 10, 2026.
records.lesson: Approval is not the end of entitlement risk. Track completion deadlines and conditions as project controls, not legal fine print.
records.sourceLabel: NYC City Record / BSA hearing notice

records.agency: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
records.observed: A 2026 BSA hearing notice describes an application for more time to complete a previously approved variance permitting residential conversion of an existing manufacturing building after the prior construction period expired.
records.lesson: Change-of-use projects can remain exposed to entitlement timing long after the use concept is approved. Conversion sequencing should track approval expiration and certificate milestones.
records.sourceLabel: NYC City Record / BSA hearing notice

records.agency: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
records.status: Extension requested years after construction period expired
records.observed: The City Record described a request to extend time to complete a three-story office-building project under a previously granted variance whose construction period had expired in 2017, together with a waiver request.
records.lesson: A dormant or delayed project can accumulate procedural recovery work. Track entitlement dates alongside financing and construction schedules.
records.sourceLabel: NYC City Record / BSA hearing notice

records.agency: NYC Board of Standards and Appeals
records.status: Extension requested after long-expired construction period
records.observed: A 2025 BSA hearing notice described an application to extend time to complete a previously approved two-story development whose construction period had expired in 2018, together with a waiver request.
records.lesson: Long delays can turn old approvals into a fresh procedural problem. Treat entitlement maintenance as an active project responsibility.
records.sourceLabel: NYC City Record / BSA hearing notice
